findings.evidence:
- `pkg/parser/parser.y:10247` sets `nextSetOprList.AfterSetOperator = $2` while also copying `limit2/orderBy2` from embedded `*ast.SetOprStmt`, so a `*ast.SetOprSelectList` with non-nil `Limit/OrderBy` can legally have `AfterSetOperator=INTERSECT`.
- `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:2070` breaks INTERSECT grouping when `selects[i+1]` is `*ast.SetOprSelectList` with `Limit/OrderBy` (sets `breakIteration=true` at `:2081`). This can create an intersect-segment whose *first* node has `AfterSetOperator=INTERSECT`.
- `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:2227` `buildExcept()` treats any `afterSetOpts[i]` that is not `EXCEPT/EXCEPT ALL` as UNION input (`else` branch at `:2250`), and `divideUnionSelectPlans()` treats any non-`UNION ALL` as DISTINCT (`pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:2300`). So an `INTERSECT` operator leaking into `afterSetOpts` will be planned as UNION (distinct).
findings.fix: In `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go` remove the `if x.Limit != nil || x.OrderBy != nil { breakIteration = true }` guard inside the INTERSECT-precedence grouping loop (so `INTERSECT` always groups across `*ast.SetOprSelectList` operands regardless of embedded `OrderBy/Limit`). If a barrier is still desired, then `buildExcept/buildUnion` must be extended to handle `afterSetOpts[i]==INTERSECT`, but the minimal correct fix is to not break the INTERSECT grouping here.
findings.impact: Queries that use `INTERSECT` with an operand that is an embedded set-op statement carrying its own `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` (e.g. `A INTERSECT (B UNION C ORDER BY ... LIMIT ...)`) can be planned/executed with UNION semantics instead of INTERSECT, producing wrong results (SQL semantics/correctness regression).
findings.verify: Add executor+planner tests for INTERSECT with embedded set-op + order/limit, e.g. `select 1 intersect ((select 1 union select 2 order by 1 desc limit 1))` should return empty; and a variant where inner topN returns `1` should return `1`. Also add a plan test to ensure the top-level operator remains INTERSECT (not UNION).
findings.what: Planner regression: `buildSetOpr()` breaks INTERSECT-precedence grouping when encountering a `*ast.SetOprSelectList` that has embedded `OrderBy/Limit`, which can cause the INTERSECT operator to be misrouted into the UNION/EXCEPT stage and executed as UNION (distinct) instead of INTERSECT.

subject: parser, planner: fix embedded setOprStmt will be seen as SetOprSelectList item and lost its orderBy and Limit (#49421)
summary: Found 1 remaining Blocker: `buildSetOpr()` can mis-handle `INTERSECT` when the right operand is an embedded set-op carrying `ORDER BY/LIMIT`, effectively planning it as UNION. This behavior still exists on `pingcap/master`.
